title: Cost Commentary Studio — pricing annotations & token-level export UX
creator: Asha Patel
description: Design and prototype a lightweight ‘Cost Commentary Studio’ in the Redwood Console: an annotatable panel layered on token-level cost analytics that supports inline pricing notes, exportable attribution slices, and role-aware export controls. Goal is to give PMs and finance teams a way to attach human-readable rationale to anomalous cost rows, capture exportable context for audits, and preview how rounding/aggregation policies affect downstream invoices.
comments: 2026-03-02 - Kickoff: scoped studio to three focused flows: (1) single-invocation drill (token sparkline + prompt diff), (2) route-level attribution slices (grouped by model + route + user segment), (3) export pipeline (CSV/JSON + audit metadata). Linked rough wireframes in Figma.

2026-03-05 - Research: chatted with 3 finance customers and 2 platform engineers. Key ask: exports must include stable identifiers (route_id, model_snapshot_id, prompt_id) and a human note field. Concern from infra: export generation at scale must be asynchronous and permission-checked.

2026-03-08 - Design review with PM and Eng: proposed UI pattern: compact table rows with micro-sparkline, hover-to-expand token breakdown, right-rail commentary panel. Trade-offs discussed: embedding full comment editor in table vs. a dedicated slide-over. Decision: use slide-over to keep table performance predictable.

2026-03-10 - Prototype: high-fidelity Figma prototype created (link below). Implemented three annotation modes: private note, shared comment, and system-tag (auto-tag anomalies). UX note: shared comments are versioned and show creator/timestamp.

2026-03-12 - Security review request: exports flagged for potential sensitive prompt content. Proposed mitigations: default redaction toggle, export audit log, and role-gated export permission. Submitted SR ticket to Security (SEC-1042).

2026-03-13 - Engineering sync: backend will expose an export job API (jobs/export-costs) that accepts filters, aggregation_level, include_prompt_text boolean. Estimated infra effort: 2 sprint days to add permission checks and async job queueing.

2026-03-14 - Design QA: tightened copy for pricing heuristics tooltip (how rounding and proration is applied). Added example rows showing pre/post-aggregation differences for a multi-model canary rollout.
2026-03-15 - In Review: seeking design review from Console PM (Jia Chen) and Head of Finance Tools (Liam O’Connor). Also requesting privacy sign-off from Security team on redaction flows.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype: slide-over comment editor and per-row micro-sparkline are implemented in Figma and clickable flows demonstrated.
Export: export jobs accept filters and return CSV and compact JSON that include stable IDs, aggregation policy metadata, and comment payloads (when allowed).
Security: export redaction toggle implemented in prototype and Security sign-off documented.
Performance: table interactions maintain <100ms perceived latency for the first 50 rows; slide-over loads lazily.
UX: annotation states (private/shared/system) visible and searchable; shared comments are included in an exportable audit trail.
Developer handoff: redlines and component spec added to Console component library doc with token-level rendering rules.
decision_log: Use slide-over for commentary editing to avoid heavy inline editors in virtualized tables.
Expose a redaction toggle for prompt text in exports; default to redacted for non-admin roles.
Support three annotation classes: private note (user-only), shared comment (team-visible), system-tag (auto-applied by monitoring).
Aggregation will support two policies: per-invocation (fine-grain token rows) and per-route (summarized). Both export formats must include policy metadata so downstream billing can reproduce numbers.
Export generation must be asynchronous with job status UI and audit logs; exports are kept for 30 days by default.
